response:
Final-round diagnosis. Scoring the whole archive on the joint criterion, the frontier is: liquidity-conditioned net external financing (fmb −5.34, alpha −3.3%, t −3.19, Sharpe −0.32), the dual-market conjunction (alpha −3.8%, t −3.16, fmb −2.47), and their stacked form (fmb −4.29, alpha −3.1%). Gen-8 sharpened two things. First, *real-activity conditioners work only on the expansion side*: capacity growth gave fmb −5.59 / alpha −2.3% and payroll growth −5.56 / −2.0%, while capacity contraction gave alpha −0.1% — so the mechanism is empire building among expanders, not distress financing. Second, *firm-type conditioners (goodwill stock, intangible intensity, inventory build) produce strong slopes with negligible alpha*, i.e. they are spanned by FF5 loadings; only slack-type and real-expansion conditioners deliver abnormal returns. Since no single-weight variant has beaten −3.3%, the remaining upside lies in (i) the *measured financing quantity* — gross intake beat net (−2.8% vs −3.3% with a different slope profile) and channel breadth produced the largest alpha — and (ii) *how two strong weights are combined*, where every MIN conjunction thinned the tails and lost alpha. This batch therefore builds one new financing quantity (breadth of gross intake), tests the product combiner against the failed MIN combiner, and adds three previously untested predetermined states.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Breadth of gross capital intake under liquidity
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(LAG(che, 1), LAG(at, 1))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MIN(RATIO(sstk, LAG(at, 1)), RATIO(dltis, LAG(at, 1))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Discretionary capital accumulation is best measured by the smaller of what a firm takes in from shareholders and from creditors, before any netting of contractual repayments: if even the lesser channel is large, the firm is deliberately pulling money in on both fronts, and doing so while already liquid is opportunism rather than project finance.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This fuses the archive's two most productive financing-leg discoveries into a single new measured quantity rather than swapping components: gross intake avoids letting mandatory debt retirement offset discretionary raising (which improved alpha to −2.8%), and the channel-breadth conjunction is what generated the largest alpha in the archive (−3.8%). Because the minimum is taken over gross, non-negative flows before standardization, the resulting variable is far less skewed than the earlier minimum of two net z-scores, which is the specific defect that held that signal's slope to −2.47.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Accelerating buildout funded from markets
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(ACCEL(GROWTH(ppegt, 1))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose capacity growth is not merely high but accelerating are late in their own expansion cycle, when project quality is deteriorating and optimism peaks; financing that acceleration from capital markets is the moment at which empire building is most likely to destroy value, while decelerating firms that retire securities are rationally winding down.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Gen-8 established that the expansion side of the capital-stock change carries the effect (alpha −2.3%, fmb −5.59) and the contraction side does not (−0.1%), so the natural sharpening is the second derivative — a temporal concept no archive entry has used — which distinguishes firms still adding to their growth rate from those merely maintaining one. Acceleration is also far less collinear with the level of asset growth that CMA prices, which is the plausible reason the level-based real conditioners stalled near −2%.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Round tripping by comfortable firms
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(LAG(che, 1), LAG(at, 1))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(LAG(dvc, 1), LAG(prstkc, 1)), LAG(at, 1)))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm that is liquid and has an established habit of large distributions has demonstrated twice over that it does not need outside money; raising capital anyway means money is coming in one door and going out another, a round trip that serves timing or optics rather than investment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The payout-commitment state is measured from *lagged* distributions so it is predetermined, unlike the gen-4 dividend-over-investment conditioner that mixed contemporaneous policy with the raise and produced only −0.4%; combining it multiplicatively with liquidity keeps both weights continuous instead of imposing the MIN conjunctions that repeatedly thinned the extreme portfolios and cost alpha. The economic claim — capital round-tripping among unconstrained firms — is distinct from both pure slack and real-expansion stories.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Raising capital at the peak of the own investment cycle
EXPRESSION: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(capx, COALESCE(aqc, 0)), at), 5), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Investment programs are cyclical within a firm, and the top of a firm's own five-year spending cycle is when management is most confident and least discriminating; funding that peak from capital markets marks the point of maximum overextension, whereas a firm at its own investment trough returning capital is exercising restraint.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Firm-relative conditioning has been tested only on liquidity, where it produced the archive's best Sharpe (−0.36) with a strong slope (−5.35); applying it to the investment program measures cycle position rather than the cross-sectional capital intensity that industry ranks largely absorb. It also avoids the level-based capex weight whose cross-sectional version left alpha near −2%, because the within-firm rank removes the permanent business-model component of the investment rate.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Liquid expanders raising capital with smooth weighting
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(LAG(che, 1), LAG(at, 1))), IND_RANK(GROWTH(ppegt, 1))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The empire-building configuration is a firm that has ample cash, is expanding its productive base, and still takes money from investors; both conditions should matter jointly, but the strength of the warning should scale smoothly with each rather than being set by whichever is weaker.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Every attempt to combine two conditioning states in this archive used MIN, and each time the alpha fell relative to the single-conditioner benchmark (−3.3% to −2.3%, −2.0%, −3.1%) because the extreme portfolios became thin; the product of two continuous [0,1] ranks preserves a broad, smoothly graded weight while still requiring both conditions, so this is a combiner-structure test with a clear prior rather than a component reshuffle. Its two parents are the strongest slack conditioner (alpha −3.3%) and the strongest real-expansion conditioner (fmb −5.59, alpha −2.3%), which are economically and statistically distinct dimensions.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Capital raised on top of last years cash build
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(LAG(che, 1), LAG(che, 2)), LAG(at, 2))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm whose cash balance rose last year and which raises fresh outside capital this year is accumulating resources sequentially without deploying them; the prior build proves the previous inflow was not needed, so the new raise is opportunistic accumulation rather than funding of a shortfall.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive's one attempt to use a cash *change* alongside financing was contemporaneous and additive and gave contrary evidence (alpha +1.5%), whereas here the build is strictly predetermined — measured entirely before the financing year — which turns it into a state that can condition rather than a mechanical accounting counterpart of the raise. It targets the dynamic version of the "no need" story that the static cash level captures only imperfectly, and both inputs are dense balance-sheet items so coverage should match the archive's norm.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Breadth of gross capital intake under liquidity---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is essentially the intersection of two existing archive entries ("Liquid firms tapping both markets at once" and "Gross capital intake by liquid firms") with only the net→gross swap inside the MIN, and the claimed skewness fix is backwards — MIN of two non-negative, zero-inflated gross flows will be pinned at or near zero for a large share of firms, thinning dispersion rather than improving it, while gross dltis is dominated by mechanical rollover rather than discretionary accumulation.

---CRITIQUE Accelerating buildout funded from markets---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The temporal second-derivative angle is genuinely new to this archive and economically defensible, but the expression is inconsistent with the stated hypothesis ("not merely high but accelerating"): IND_RANK(ACCEL(GROWTH(ppegt))) assigns top ranks to firms whose growth merely became less negative, i.e. exactly the contracting group that gen-8 showed carries no effect, so a level floor on capacity growth is needed before this is a clean test (and the standalone leg overlaps the published investment-growth/abnormal-capital-investment anomaly).

---CRITIQUE Round tripping by comfortable firms---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The round-tripping story was already tested in gen-4 with a payout conditioner and failed on the portfolio side (alpha −0.4%), and lagging the payout term plus multiplying by the liquidity rank does not create a new economic state — payout habit is largely a proxy for the maturity/slack dimension the liquidity leg already captures, so this is a near-duplicate rather than a substantively different mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Raising capital at the peak of the own investment cycle---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: It is a conditioner swap on the archive's dominant backbone, but firm-relative investment-cycle position is an economically distinct state from cross-sectional investment intensity and from own-liquidity rank, and it is internally coherent; the main caveats are that the standalone conditioner is close to the published Titman-Wei-Xie abnormal capital investment measure and that the archive's evidence (liquid low-investment raisers performed strongest) argues against the peak-investment premise.

---CRITIQUE Liquid expanders raising capital with smooth weighting---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a combiner-mechanics variant, not a new mechanism: both conditioners are already in the archive and the product of two [0,1] ranks is a near-monotone re-weighting of the MIN construction it replaces, so any improvement would be cosmetic and hard to interpret economically.

---CRITIQUE Capital raised on top of last years cash build---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Using a strictly predetermined cash *build* rather than the contemporaneous cash change is a legitimate and non-mechanical reformulation of the "no funding need" state, though the incremental content over the static cash level and over multi-year issuance persistence is likely modest since last year's cash build is itself largely a product of last year's issuance.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Funds raised beyond contractual repayment need
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(LAG(che, 1), LAG(at, 1))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), dltr), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Debt repayment is contractual and share repurchase is discretionary, so the two should not be treated symmetrically: the correct measure of discretionary accumulation is what a firm brought in from both markets minus only what it was obliged to repay, and a liquid firm accumulating on that basis is taking capital it demonstrably does not need.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This abandons the zero-inflated MIN of gross flows the critic correctly identified as dispersion-destroying and instead defines a new financing quantity that sits between the archive's two tested legs — gross intake (alpha −2.8%) and fully netted flow (−3.3%) — by removing rollover mechanics from the numerator while refusing to let buybacks cancel issuance. The economic distinction is discretion versus obligation, and because repurchases now push firms toward the long tail only through the absence of intake, the two extremes remain "accumulating despite slack" versus "quietly self-funding".

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Externally funded acceleration of an expanding base
EXPRESSION: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(GROWTH(ppegt, 1)), IND_RANK(ACCEL(GROWTH(ppegt, 1)))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The dangerous state is capacity growth that is both high and still accelerating — a firm late in its own buildout, adding to an already rising growth rate — and financing that state from capital markets marks peak managerial optimism; firms whose growth is merely becoming less negative are contracting and, as the archive shows, carry no such penalty.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The MIN over the growth level and its acceleration installs exactly the level floor the critique demanded, so top weights require genuine expansion *and* rising momentum rather than a mechanical arithmetic artifact of decelerating contraction. This keeps the batch's only new temporal concept while making the expression faithful to the hypothesis, and it separates the signal from the standalone abnormal-capital-investment anomaly because a high investment level alone does not qualify a firm for the high-weight group.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Capacity expansion paid for with paper
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(GROWTH(ppegt, 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: When a firm grows its productive base while its share count grows in step, the expansion is being bought with newly printed ownership claims rather than with cash the business generated, so existing shareholders finance scale that does not raise per-share capacity; the mirror case, capacity growth alongside share retirement, is genuinely self-funded expansion.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This replaces the failed round-tripping story with the last untested major channel pair, and it is motivated by the archive's most reliable structural lesson: the payroll-and-financing pair produced contrary positive alpha as an additive rank composite (+2.0%) yet correctly signed alpha (−2.0%, t −2.12) once recast as a signed conditional, and the dilution-and-capacity pair has so far only been tested additively (+1.9% to +2.0%). Both inputs are dense balance-sheet items with no accounting overlap, so coverage should be at the top of the archive's range and the interaction cannot be mechanical.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Market funded expansion beyond the installed base
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(capx, COALESCE(aqc, 0)), LAG(ppent, 1)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Spending measured against the capital already installed, rather than against total assets, identifies firms attempting to build something several times the size of what they currently operate; such leaps are the least validated by operating experience, and funding them from capital markets is the clearest empire-building configuration.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This drops the combiner-mechanics variant and instead changes the normalization of the investment state itself — the reinvestment rate on installed plant, never used as a conditioner in the archive, where every investment weight has been scaled by total assets and stalled near alpha −2.3%. The rescaling shifts weight from capital-intensive incumbents toward firms whose spending dwarfs their existing operations, which is where the overextension mechanism should be strongest, and the rank transform makes the weight robust to small-denominator observations without contaminating any cross-sectional standardization.
